text: Güicán de la Sierra, also known as Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria de Güicán, is a town and municipality located in the Colombian Department of Boyacá. It is situated near the national natural park El Cocuy National Park. As of 2020, the municipality has a total population of 6,426. The municipality is named after the Güicán tribe, an indigenous group that once inhabited the region and is related to the U'wa people; the name Güicán translates to "in the fence of the wife" in the indigenous language. The Spanish conquistador Hernán Pérez de Quesada arrived in the area in search of gold, and the indigenous people retreated behind the Sierra Nevada to avoid him. The municipality was officially founded by Jesuit friar Miguel Blasco on February 26, 1756. It shares borders with Chiscas and Cubará to the north, Fortul and Saravena to the east, Tame and El Cocuy to the south, and Panqueba and El Espino to the west. The average elevation of Güicán is 3,492 meters above sea level. The region has a Tundra Climate (ET), with the highest average rainfall occurring in April at 244 mm and the lowest in January at 83 mm.
